**Root cause:** The docs deploy workflow's "Resolve changed docs" step runs `docs/scripts/changed-pages.ts` directly with `node`. That script statically imports `@pantoken/i18n-engine`, whose `exports` map points at `dist/index.mjs` — but nothing had built that package yet on a fresh checkout, so it failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Every other place in the repo that needs `@pantoken/i18n-engine` (e.g. [ci.yml](/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L662)'s `vp run -r build`) builds workspace packages first; this step didn't.

**Fix:** Added a `Build changed-pages script dependencies` step (`vp run -F "@pantoken/i18n-engine..." build`) before "Resolve changed docs" in [.github/workflows/docs.yml](/.github/workflows/docs.yml#L182-L187). Verified locally by deleting `tools/i18n-engine/dist` and confirming `changed-pages.ts` fails before the build step and succeeds after it. The subsequent `vp run -F "@pantoken/docs..." build` steps depend on the same package, so they'll hit this build's cache rather than duplicating work.

Opened [PR #148](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken/pull/148) with the comprehensive fix.

## Root cause
The previous fix only built `@pantoken/i18n-engine` before the "Resolve changed docs" step. But `changed-pages.ts` and `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts` (which it imports) pull in **multiple** workspace packages' built `dist` output directly (e.g. `@pantoken/web-components`), not just `i18n-engine` — so the same class of `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` recurred on the next unbuilt dependency.

## Fix
Replaced the narrow, single-package build step with `vp run -F "@pantoken/docs..." build` — building `@pantoken/docs`'s **entire** dependency graph up front, matching what the later build steps in the same job already do (so no extra cost; it's a cache hit there).

Verified locally by deleting `dist` for `@pantoken/i18n-engine`, `@pantoken/translation-adapters`, and `@pantoken/web-components` simultaneously, running the new build step, and confirming `changed-pages.ts` executes successfully.

Also added a `@pantoken/docs` changeset describing the fix, following repo convention of changelogging internal package fixes.
